findings.title: Dynamic imports still execute eagerly at module load, defeating async/code-splitting goal
findings.body: The appStore object stores `import("./x")` expressions directly as object values. Since `import()` calls are evaluated immediately when the object literal is constructed (i.e., as soon as this module is loaded), all app packages are still being imported eagerly at module-load time, exactly as before. Wrapping access sites in `await appStore[key]` only defers *resolution* of already-started imports, not the import itself. This means the PR's stated purpose (async/lazy-loading of app packages to reduce bundle size) is not actually achieved — it only adds async overhead (promises, awaits) throughout the codebase without any lazy-loading benefit. To truly lazy-load, the import should occur inside a function/getter invoked only when the app is actually needed.

findings.title: Sequential awaits in for-loop serialize dynamic imports
findings.body: getVideoAdapters now loops over credentials with a `for...of` and `await appStore[appName]` inside the loop body. Each dynamic import is awaited one at a time instead of being kicked off in parallel (e.g., via Promise.all), so for multiple credentials the imports/resolutions are serialized, adding unnecessary latency compared to the previous synchronous array reduce. This is a performance regression for calls with multiple credentials (e.g., getBusyVideoTimes with many video credentials).

findings.title: forEach with async callback silently swallows errors and runs unawaited
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` was changed to await `getCalendar` inside the callback, but `forEach` does not wait for the returned promises nor propagate rejections to the enclosing try/catch. Any error thrown inside the async callback (e.g., from `getCalendar` or `calendar.deleteEvent`) becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of being caught by the surrounding `try/catch`, and the subsequent code (sending reschedule emails) does not wait for calendar/video deletions to complete before proceeding. This existed before but is now more clearly broken since `getCalendar` is async and genuinely needs awaiting across multiple iterations.

findings.title: Same forEach-async unhandled-rejection issue as vital/reschedule.ts
findings.body: Identical pattern: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` with an awaited `getCalendar` call inside. Errors are not caught by the surrounding try/catch, and the loop's async work is not awaited before the function proceeds to send emails and return, risking race conditions and silently dropped failures when deleting calendar/video references during reschedule.

findings.title: requestReschedule forEach(async) not awaited, errors unhandled
findings.body: In `requestReschedule`, `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` now awaits `getCalendar` inside, but the surrounding code does not await the forEach's async work at all (no Promise.all), and there is no try/catch around it (unlike the vital/wipemycalother examples). This can lead to unhandled promise rejections and the reschedule email being sent before calendar/video deletions actually complete, since nothing waits for them.

findings.title: forEach(async) inside calendar deletion loop not awaited
findings.body: In the recurring-event cancellation branch, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => {...})` performs awaited `getCalendar` calls and pushes to `apiDeletes` from within an async callback that forEach does not wait on. Although `apiDeletes` is later awaited via Promise.all, the push itself happens asynchronously after forEach has already returned, so there's a window where `apiDeletes` may not yet contain all the deletion promises before the outer code proceeds to use the array (e.g., `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))`), risking some deletions being missed from the final await.
